facts.statement: The only species, Lusitanisuchus mitracostatus, was named in 2004 after previously being described as Lisboasaurus in 1970.
facts.quote: The only species, Lusitanisuchus mitracostatus, was named in 2004 after having previously been described as a species of the genus Lisboasaurus in 1970.

facts.statement: A later reexamination of fossils from the Guimarota Formation found skull material, including a dentary similar to the holotype, proving it was a crocodylomorph rather than a lizard.
facts.quote: However, a later reexamination of fossils from the Guimarota Formation had found skull material that included a dentary similar to the one seen in the holotype of L. mitracostatus.

facts.statement: Teeth found at Porto Dinheiro, Lourinhã in Berriasian strata extend the known temporal range of the taxon by about 15 million years.
facts.quote: Several teeth referable to Lusitanisuchus were also found from Porto Dinheiro, Lourinhã in strata deposited during the Berriasian stage of the Early Cretaceous, extending the temporal range of this taxon by about 15 Ma.

facts.statement: The genus lived from 152.21 to 149.2 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Lusitanisuchus coexisted with many dinosaurs in the Lusitanian Basin during the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Lusitanisuchus coexisted with many dinosaurs from the Lusitanian Basin during the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The parent group of Lusitanisuchus is Mesoeucrocodylia.
Lusitanisuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
